correspondence.finding: La Soledad / Salto de las Vacas intermittent-drainage terrain west of Sierra la Centella is positively mapped. The following regional corridor includes the El Rosario–Los Barriales–Sabana Grande setting. Local reach labels are not extended over the full object.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward terrain and local drainage read; full joining sequence is not established.

correspondence.finding: The route proceeds through the Santa Rita / Guadalupe intervening valley and north/east Guadalupe footslope setting. Adjacent Arroyo Grande / Mazapil-side drainage arrives from the east near Cedros; it is distinct from the selected southern opening.

correspondence.finding: The selected diagonal traverses the broad Bajío La Lagunita–Bajío Malatierra–Barrial San José alluvial setting. Short mapped watercourses terminate separately; tanks and track/road junctions do not establish the selected through-going watercourse.
correspondence.correspondence: Material connector unresolved despite original map coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: El Vergel / Matamoros to Salitrillo map transition
correspondence.finding: Intermittent drainage and alluvial terrain are read through the northwestern Concepción del Oro map sector and the northeastern Juan Aldama corner beside Salitrillo and Sierra El Cajón. A locality label is not a river-name assignment.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected regional transition examined; it cannot repair the central flat gap.

correspondence.finding: La Tinaja / Chapulin local drainage and the intervening sierras and Llanos Menchaca / Bajo Los Llanos setting are mapped. Their local names and course ends remain distinct from the longer selected modeled system.
correspondence.correspondence: Northern regional corridor read, representative identity unestablished.

correspondence.finding: The selected terminal hook and ending occupy the plain east of Viesca, around the Cuadro Salino–Estación Bilbao–Llano Los Torreones setting. Detailed cartography shows lacustrine terrain and infrastructure but no continuous selected final watercourse. The separate mapped Laguna de Viesca is not silently used as the endpoint or receiving lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Terminal terrain positive; selected channel/flat continuation materially unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern headward opening and initial lake/stream chain
correspondence.finding: Selected geometry supplies orientation for an east-to-west opening followed by a southward chain in the northern 25D sector. None of the usable primary originals covers and distinguishes this actual headward lake entrance, outlet and connecting stream sequence. Lac Buet and the neighboring eastern lake are discovery leads only and are not assigned to the selected passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper southwestward corridor and intermediate lake/tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestward corridor, intermediate elongated-waterbody passages and tributary confluences are outside the sufficiently legible coverage of the usable ecological map. Failed regional reports and the denied NTS025D original provide no map evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Western bend and middle eastward continuation
correspondence.finding: The ecological location map supplies regional orientation north of the separate Vachon and Arnaud waterways but does not establish the selected western bend and each continuation through the lake-rich middle corridor at ordinary component scale. Unknown lake and feeder names remain null.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southeastward bend, eastward river corridor and material lateral junctions
correspondence.finding: The printed-page3 original identifies the lower Buet corridor north of the Arnaud estuary and depicts its bending eastward approach, distinct from the Vachon confluence farther west. This supports a lower-corridor candidate, but the regional relief map does not fully distinguish all selected lake outlets and lateral tributary junctions. Names from discovery-only records are not attached to the unresolved junctions.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southward approach and Arnaud-estuary terminal setting
correspondence.finding: At ordinary generalized corridor scale, the original location map shows the named Buet lower valley turning toward and joining the north side of the wide Arnaud estuarine waterway west of Kangirsuk. Printed-page102 prose separately identifies Buet among the Arnaud tributary valleys and places the upstream tidal limit at the Vachon mouth. The selected terminal belongs to that estuarine receiving-water setting; no exact bank, mouth vertex, named bay or tidal boundary is claimed.

The selected headward component begins in the western Lost Reindeer lake setting and takes a short southern/eastward transfer into the easterly lake before turning north. NLUIS107B depicts both lakes and nearby marshes, streams and pools, but the complete selected inter-lake transfer is not securely traceable. The GRRB prose records uncertain or differing broader drainage interpretations rather than proving this connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Lost Reindeer lake and northern pond/stream approach
correspondence.finding: The easterly named lake’s northern continuation passes through small pools and marshy stream connections, then bends northwest/west before entering the northward river corridor. These source features correspond to the selected headward course beyond the unresolved transfer. The lake and unnamed connecting reaches are not all renamed Miner River.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Miner corridor east of Sitidgi Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected stream runs north then northeast through a lake-dotted upland east of Sitidgi Lake, crossing into the adjacent eastern map sheet. Original107B shows the watercourse and ordinary tributary joins; DFOFigure1 distinguishes this southwestern approach as Miner River from the Kugaluk approach farther east. Sitidgi Lake is a neighboring basin and is not inserted into this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Miner valley and northern Crossley sheet continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected northeastward course follows the western river corridor on107A, widens into a meandering low valley, makes the pronounced western/northern turn and continues north to the adjoining Stanton sheet. Original water lines, floodplain pools and tributary joins are readable throughout this sector. The separately incised Kugaluk River corridor farther east is not substituted for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Miner and Kugaluk River junction setting
correspondence.finding: On107D the lower Miner corridor approaches from the southwest through meanders and floodplain waterbodies. The source distinguishes the Kugaluk River arriving from the south/east and shows their connections into the shared lower estuarine waterway. The selected route follows that junction setting northward; no exact distributary-bank or mouth-vertex choice is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Kugaluk Channel continuation and actual selected coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The selection continues north through the narrow branching estuarine inlet into its wider tidal-water setting south of Thumb Island and southeast of the Husky Lakes fingers. Original107D covers the actual selected terminal setting, and DFO identifies this inlet as Kugaluk Channel at the southwestern end of Liverpool Bay, including the Miner and Kugaluk mouths. The selection does not run to the open Beaufort Sea coast or to the separate Husky Lakes opening northwest of Thumb Island.

This mixed-name-scope fragment begins on the mapped unnamed southern feeder. Its initial northeastward course turns north and joins the Rio Jacundá approach on the southern sheet. The selected course then follows repeatedly labelled Rio Jacundá northward, with westward bends and lateral feeder joins, across the two-sheet transition and farther northwest toward the broader channel. Every selected headward and intermediate connector is depicted; no missing lake or wetland link is assumed. Rio Jacundá is representative of this downstream connected system, but the fragment is not uniformly named because its initial feeder hydronym is unestablished.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The northern fragment continues on the same Rio Jacundá course from the preceding fragment, heading northwest through a wider channel with island-side passages, including the Papagaio/Macaquinho setting. It then trends north along the Jacundá side of Ilha Taquari; the separately labelled Taquari waterway branches to the east. The selected terminal lies beside the northeast side of Ilha Mirituba, south of Ilha Jacundá, at the transition to Baía das Bocas in the Rio Pará estuarine network. No named lake/reservoir passage or geographically unestablished connector remains.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete through actual selected terminal at ordinary generalized corridor scale
